The Quantile of a Symmetric Family on the Log Scale

Source: R/pseudohuber_distrib.R
symmetric_log_quantile.Rd

Returns the quantile of a law symmetric about its first parameter, solved on the logarithm of the smaller tail: the root of \(\log F(q) = \log p\) is found below the location by stats::uniroot() and reflected about it when the upper tail is the smaller one, so that the computation forms neither \(1 - p\) nor \(\exp(\log p)\). The two pseudo-Huber families use it.

Usage

symmetric_log_quantile(distrib, p, theta, lower.tail, log.p, spread)

Arguments

distrib

A distribution object symmetric about its first parameter.

p

A numeric vector of probabilities, or their logarithms.

theta

A named list of parameter values.

lower.tail, log.p

Logical of length 1.

spread

A function of the parameter list that sets the width of the first bracket, which is doubled until it contains the root.

Value

A numeric vector of quantiles.

Examples

d <- pseudohuber_distrib()
distributions7:::symmetric_log_quantile(d, 1e-30, list(mu = 0, sigma = 1, nu = 2),
                                        FALSE, FALSE, function(th) th[[2]])
#> [1] 69.18132
